chapter: Trumpet technique: breath, lip and effects
title: Vibrato and effects among Oliver, Bunk, Kelly, Morgan and Armstrong
summary: Punch says who shook the horn, used a plunger or kept steady, recalls hearing Oliver in Chicago, and describes country trumpeters.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Lips, teeth and breath: the physical craft of brass playing

blocks.x: No, but now what about people like, I'll say King Oliver and Joe Howard and Buddy Petit and all the, Chris Kelly, all the different ones you remember. Do you remember how they would produce those different effects? Yeah. Like, would they shake their hands, any of them? But, if he did.
He shook his hands.
Yeah.

But, uh, a fellow like Bunk, I don't know, I went on an excursion one time. First time I was a young kid, then saw him play and he used to do that, but Bunk held his horn steady. And he made all kind of different ways on the song, different songs on his horn.
Mm-hmm.
But he didn't shake it or nothing.
He used to just lift.
Just lift, yeah, just lift.
Unless he growled, and you can't make a growl with just your lip. No. You gotta growl.
Mm-hmm. But I got growl, I was sitting right side some guy, and I heard him right in the ear. Mm-hmm. And the horn was going just like he was going, mm-hmm, in his throat.
Who else, uh, would, uh, use vibrato? Do you remember how Chris Kelly, Sam Morgan, anybody else?
Well, them fellas didn't use no vibrato. They just played the horn, that's all I can say. What you looking with that?
Ten. What does that sound?
Chris Kelly was strictly a plunger man, you know. Mm-hmm. And Sam just played a straight horn. I never heard him use no vibrato at all. Mm-hmm. Just played a straight horn.
What about Louis Armstrong?
Well, yeah, he used all that stuff.
Him. Mm-hmm. How would Joe Oliver do it?

Well, Joe Oliver did too. It's like I'm telling you, I didn't know much about him. The only time I saw Joe, when I first went to Chicago, I went to a place to call the plantation. Uh-huh. And I went to the Yuddy Band and I went there and heard him. But I didn't know him personally at all. I didn't know Joe Oliver.
What about out in the country? Did they play trumpet pretty much the same as in the city? Did they use the same tricks?

Well, not them days. They didn't. They were strictly musicians like Paul Rose and Mike Taylor, Spencer Taylor's name. They put that music up there and just played parades and things. They didn't play no dance music. They played parades and things. What about half-elvin? Did they do that much in those days?
